answer: A basalt foundation: each identity must wander a fixed route of independent checkpoints, starting at a jetty where a peer stamps its first basalt token, and each later checkpoint only accepts the token from the previous one, in order, with a time gap between stamps. A fake can copy one token, but it cannot copy the ordered route or skip ahead, and a farm cannot share one route across a thousand fakes because each route is bound to one identity and each stamp needs its own real visit; a thousand fakes need a thousand separately wandered routes.
